title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 650bis-787 of the sequel to La Longue Marche). Grothendieck has a profinite 'Galois-Teichmüller system' Π ⊂ 𝔊 → M. Here Π is the profinite Teichmüller (mapping-class) group, 𝔊 is its arithmetic extension, and M is a Galois-type quotient carrying a cyclotomic character. He is defining a 'Lie approximation' of it: affine algebraic groups over Q, Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q → M_Q, with M → M_Q(A_Q) satisfying conditions 1°-4° on the previous page.

On this page he brings in the 'tori' T_0. These are the free abelian subgroups (41) T_0 → Π, presumably generated by Dehn twists along a maximal system of disjoint curves, i.e. the inertia groups at the maximally degenerate points at infinity of the moduli stack.

1. Composing with Π → Π_Q(Q) gives (42) T_0 → Π_Q(Q). By a monodromy-type result (his (21), p. 747') this homomorphism is quasi-unipotent.
2. A commuting family of unipotent elements in a linear algebraic group in characteristic 0 extends uniquely, via exp/log, to a homomorphism from the vector group. Hence one gets a morphism of group schemes (43) K_i : T_{0,Q} = G_{a,Q} ⊗_Z T_0 → Π_Q. Taking Q-points recovers (42), at least on a finite-index subgroup.
3. Since there are only finitely many conjugacy classes of such maximal tori (finitely many combinatorial types of pants decompositions; same count for Π_0 or for the profinite Π), one gets a finite family K_i indexed by these classes.
4. He proposes to add to the definition of a Lie approximation the requirement that these homomorphisms be injective, i.e. monomorphisms (44) G_a ⊗ T_0 ↪ Π_Q. In words: the multitwist lattices must survive with full rank as unipotent vector subgroups.
5. He then passes to integral structures. Suppose M_Q comes from an affine group scheme of finite type M over Z with M → M(Ẑ) (45); he thinks such an M exists. The next page takes the schematic closures Π, 𝔊 of Π_Q, 𝔊_Q in M and forms the quotients T, Γ, N over Z, with representability attributed to Raynaud. It gets factorizations Π_0 → Π(Z), M → M(Ẑ), and requires the character χ: M_Q → G_m to extend to M → G_{m,Z}, factoring through Γ.

The aim is an algebraic (and even Z-integral) model of the Galois action on Teichmüller groups in which the Dehn-twist inertia is visible as embedded vector groups. This is an early version of what later became relative and weighted completion of mapping class groups and of the Galois group (Hain; Hain-Matsumoto), and of motivic and pro-unipotent approaches to the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group.
errors: Quasi-unipotence only gives unipotence on a finite-index subgroup T_0' of T_0. The morphism G_a ⊗ T_0 → Π_Q is then determined by T_0' (since G_a⊗T_0 = G_a⊗T_0'), but it reproduces (42) on Q-points only if the image of T_0 itself is unipotent. Otherwise it agrees only on T_0', with a finite-order discrepancy. The phrase 'qui définit, par passage aux pts Q-rationnels, (42)' is slightly overstated unless unipotence (not just quasi-unipotence) is assumed.
Next page: Π_0 → Π(Z) needs compatibility of Π_0 → Π_Q(Q) with M → M(Ẑ) so that the image lies in M(Q) ∩ M(Ẑ) = M(Z). This is implicit, not proved.

Representability of the quotients over Z is only asserted ('par Raynaud il n'y a jamais de pb'). Over a Dedekind base, results of Raynaud and Anantharaman give representability, sometimes only as an algebraic space in general. This is a minor gap.
Existence of an integral model M with M → M(Ẑ) is only conjectured ('il me semble qu'on peut...').

ideas.what: Dehn-multitwist 'tori' T_0 in the Teichmüller group map quasi-unipotently into the algebraic approximation, hence give G_a ⊗ T_0 → Π_Q.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy theorem / unipotent image of Dehn twists in relative (Malcev) completion of mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain (relative completion of mapping class groups, 1990s); quasi-unipotent monodromy is classical (Grothendieck, Landman, Borel)
ideas.where_published: Tori/multitwists appear in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; this algebraic-group version is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Adding to the definition of 'Lie approximation' the condition that each maximal-torus map G_a⊗T_0 → Π_Q is a monomorphism, giving a finite family indexed by conjugacy classes of maximal tori.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness of maximal multitwist subgroups in relative/weighted completion; boundary (cusp) inertia conditions in Hain-Matsumoto
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain, Hain-Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003); related to 'inertia-preserving' conditions in GT (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura)

ideas.what: Integral model: an affine Z-group scheme M with M → M(Ẑ), and schematic closures of Π_Q, 𝔊_Q in M forming an exact diagram of flat Z-group schemes with a cyclotomic character M → G_{m,Z}.
ideas.modern_name: Integral models of (weighted/motivic) completions; integral motivic fundamental group / Z-structures on Lie approximations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Partly Deligne (Z-structures on motivic π1 of P^1-{0,1,∞}), Brown; no general Z-integral version for Teichmüller towers known to me

ideas.what: Schematic closure and representability of quotients of flat group schemes over Z.
ideas.modern_name: Schematic closure; quotients of group schemes over a Dedekind base
ideas.where_published: EGA IV and SGA 3 background (closure techniques)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an algebraic 'Lie approximation' of the Galois-Teichmüller tower. He requires as an axiom that the maximal Dehn-multitwist lattices embed as vector groups G_a⊗T_0. He then asks for a Z-integral model whose Ẑ-points receive the profinite arithmetic group. The integral program over Z for the whole Teichmüller tower appears not to have been developed.
missed.quote: Supposons que M_Q provienne d'un schéma en groupes (affine de t.f.) M sur Z, tel que l'on ait (45) M → M(Ẑ) (il me semble qu'on peut alors trouver un tel M ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Hain-Matsumoto's weighted completions are ℓ-adic or over Q. An integral (all primes simultaneously) Lie approximation of the Galois action on mapping class groups would be a new structure. It relates to integrality questions for motivic Galois groups and for GT.

missed.claim: The injectivity axiom for the maps G_a⊗T_0 → Π_Q makes a precise link between boundary inertia (degeneration tori in the Deligne-Mumford compactification) and the algebraic-group approximation. It is an 'inertia-preserving' condition imposed at the Lie-algebraic level, prefiguring the cusp/boundary conditions in weighted completion and in GRT.
missed.quote: les hom. précédents aux tores max[imaux] [soient] injectifs, donc aussi des monomorphismes (44) K_i : T_0Q ≃ G_aQ ⊗_Z T_0 ↪ Π_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives historical precedence, and possibly a cleaner axiomatization of Lie-type approximations of the Teichmüller tower using finitely many maximal-torus embeddings.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck setting up something very close to relative/weighted completion of the Galois-Teichmüller system, with Dehn-twist tori as embedded vector groups and an integral model over Z. This predates Hain and Hain-Matsumoto and is not in his published texts. The individual steps are routine, and the integral part remains conjectural and sketchy.
transcription_corrections: 'indexé par l'ens des groupes de sous-groupes ouverts de π_0' is doubtful. Context suggests 'indexé par l'ens. des classes [de conjugaison] de tores maximaux de Π_0, ou de Π (ce qui revient au même)'.

'J'ai envie d'appeler les applications ... de Lie un ens. de génération les les hom. précédents aux tores max finis' likely reads 'J'ai envie d'ajouter à la déf. des approximations de Lie la condition que les hom. précédents relatifs aux tores max. soient injectifs, donc aussi des monomorphismes (44)'. The struck word is probably 'représentations'.
'p53' over the arrow in (43) is probably a marginal page reference or label, not part of the formula.
'(pas seulement en groupes !)' probably emphasizes that (43) is a homomorphism of group schemes, not merely of abstract groups.
